response: The acceptance rates of a national preventive home visit programme for older people are indeed socially imbalanced. Research has shown that high socioeconomic status is associated with a higher acceptance rate of preventive home visits. However, this association can be attenuated by invitational procedures, suggesting that more proactive approaches to inviting participants can help reduce social inequality in acceptance of publicly offered preventive services. This means that by adopting more effective invitational procedures, municipalities may be able to decrease the social imbalance in acceptance rates and increase participation from older people across all socioeconomic backgrounds.
